name: Observed 1 of 2: Agent identity
description: Agent identity, as a real run performed it: the exchanges observed in a capture, matched to its steps. Tokens are decoded, not verified.

steps.label: Request agent token (web app)
steps.description: The agent generates a fresh ephemeral key and asks its agent provider for an agent token. It signs the request with the new key, and the Signature-Key header carries a naming JWT signed by its durable key, which vouches for the new key. The agent provider recognizes the durable key from enrollment, checks that the new key signed the request, and applies its policy.

example.note: This is the web app pattern from the AAuth Bootstrap guidance; the endpoint path is the agent provider's own. Enrollment came first: the user signed in and the agent registered its durable key. Other platforms differ: a mobile app keeps its durable key in the Secure Enclave or StrongBox and usually attests it with App Attest or Play Integrity at enrollment; a self-hosted agent publishes its own JWKS and issues its own agent token, with no request at all; workload identity is not yet covered by the guidance.

steps.curl:
# The signature headers are replayed from the example; curl cannot create HTTP message signatures.
curl -X POST 'https://agent.example/agent-token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Digest: sha-256=:RBNvo1WzZ4oRRq0W9+hknpT7T8If536DEMBg9hyq/4o=:' \
  -H 'Signature-Input: sig=("@method" "@authority" "@path" "content-type" "content-digest" "signature-key");created=1730216995' \
  -H 'Signature: sig=:SIGNATURE-PLACEHOLDER:' \
  -H 'Signature-Key: sig=jkt-jwt;jwt="eyJ0eXAiOiJqa3QtczI1Nitqd3QiLCJhbGciOiJFZDI1NTE5IiwiandrIjp7Imt0eSI6Ik9LUCIsImNydiI6IkVkMjU1MTkiLCJ4IjoiWDg5aVlfREZkRkJJWnBHdFBONFFwNWdWbzJTVXNlcHFSekVwcXZra1pLQSIsImFsZyI6IkVkMjU1MTkifX0.eyJpc3MiOi…"' \
  --data-raw '{}'

steps.label: agent_token
steps.description: The agent provider issues an agent token: a JWT naming the agent (sub), its person server (ps) and the agent's public key (cnf). Every later request is signed with the matching private key.

example.note: The agent token binds the ephemeral key (cnf) to the agent's identifier (sub). Neither draft defines this response's format; agent providers define their own. Bootstrap guidance suggests about an hour as a typical lifetime; 24 hours is the protocol's maximum.

steps.label: HTTP Sig w/ agent_token
steps.description: The agent calls the resource. The request carries an HTTP message signature made with the agent's key, and the agent token travels in the Signature-Key header.

example.note: The agent signs every request with the key in the token's cnf; the verifier checks the signature against that key.

steps.curl:
# The signature headers are replayed from the example; curl cannot create HTTP message signatures.
curl 'https://resource.example/api/documents' \
  -H 'Signature-Input: sig=("@method" "@authority" "@path" "signature-key");created=1730217610' \
  -H 'Signature: sig=:SIGNATURE-PLACEHOLDER:' \
  -H 'Signature-Key: sig=jwt;jwt="eyJhbGciOiJFZDI1NTE5IiwidHlwIjoiYWEtYWdlbnQrand0Iiwia2lkIjoiYXAta2V5LTEifQ.eyJpc3MiOi…"'

steps.label: 200 OK
steps.description: The resource verifies the agent token and checks that its key signed the request. Knowing exactly which agent is calling, it applies its own policy and answers.

example.note: The resource decides on the agent's identity alone (sub of the agent token).

name: Observed 2 of 2: PS Authorization, Challenged on the API Call
description: PS Authorization, Challenged on the API Call, as a real run performed it: the exchanges observed in a capture, matched to its steps. Tokens are decoded, not verified.

example.note: The agent token binds the ephemeral key (cnf) to the agent's identifier (sub). Neither draft defines this response's format; agent providers define their own. Bootstrap guidance suggests about an hour as a typical lifetime; 24 hours is the protocol's maximum.

steps.label: HTTP Sig w/ agent_token
steps.description: The agent calls the API directly, signing the request with its agent token, without first asking the resource what the call needs.

example.note: The agent signs every request with the key in the token's cnf; the verifier checks the signature against that key.

steps.curl:
# The signature headers are replayed from the example; curl cannot create HTTP message signatures.
curl 'https://resource.example/api/documents' \
  -H 'Signature-Input: sig=("@method" "@authority" "@path" "signature-key");created=1730217610' \
  -H 'Signature: sig=:SIGNATURE-PLACEHOLDER:' \
  -H 'Signature-Key: sig=jwt;jwt="eyJhbGciOiJFZDI1NTE5IiwidHlwIjoiYWEtYWdlbnQrand0Iiwia2lkIjoiYXAta2V5LTEifQ.eyJpc3MiOi…"'

steps.label: 401 requirement=person-token
steps.description: The resource needs to know the person behind the agent before it will decide anything. It refuses the call with 401 and an AAuth-Requirement header naming the person token it needs. The agent gets one from the person server named in its agent token.

example.note: The challenge comes on the API call itself, so the agent needs no endpoint other than the API to learn what it must present.

steps.label: POST person_token_endpoint (HTTP Sig w/ agent_token)
steps.description: The agent asks its person server for a person token for the resource it wants to call. The request is signed with the agent's key and presents the agent token, and the signature covers the body through Content-Digest.

example.note: A body sent to a PS must be covered by the signature through Content-Digest and Content-Type (§11.3.3.1). The draft's own example in §7.1 omits them.

steps.curl:
# The signature headers are replayed from the example; curl cannot create HTTP message signatures.
curl -X POST 'https://ps.example/person' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Digest: sha-256=:3U1ftIuj9LAZ1bBe/D7cdVNDtcxTj6NrBvMLg8Jwu8M=:' \
  -H 'Signature-Input: sig=("@method" "@authority" "@path" "signature-key" "content-digest" "content-type");created=1730217590' \
  -H 'Signature: sig=:SIGNATURE-PLACEHOLDER:' \
  -H 'Signature-Key: sig=jwt;jwt="eyJhbGciOiJFZDI1NTE5IiwidHlwIjoiYWEtYWdlbnQrand0Iiwia2lkIjoiYXAta2V5LTEifQ.eyJpc3MiOi…"' \
  --data-raw '{"resource":"https://resource.example","capabilities":["interaction"]}'

steps.label: person_token (aud = resource)
steps.description: The person server returns a person token: the resource as its audience, a directed identifier for the person at that resource, and the agent's key. It carries no scope; it says who, not what is allowed.

example.note: The person token names one resource (aud) and a directed identifier for the person there (sub). It carries no scope.

steps.label: HTTP Sig w/ person_token
steps.description: The agent repeats the same API call, now presenting the person token.

example.note: The person token replaces the agent token in Signature-Key. Its cnf is the same key that signs, so verification works as before.

steps.curl:
# The signature headers are replayed from the example; curl cannot create HTTP message signatures.
curl 'https://resource.example/api/documents' \
  -H 'Signature-Input: sig=("@method" "@authority" "@path" "signature-key");created=1730217610' \
  -H 'Signature: sig=:SIGNATURE-PLACEHOLDER:' \
  -H 'Signature-Key: sig=jwt;jwt="eyJhbGciOiJFZDI1NTE5IiwidHlwIjoiYWEtcGVyc29uK2p3dCIsImtpZCI6InBzLWtleS0xIn0.eyJpc3MiOi…"'

steps.label: 401 requirement=auth-token, with resource_token
steps.description: The person is known, but this call needs the person's consent or the person server's policy for a scope. The resource refuses again with 401, and its AAuth-Requirement header carries a resource token addressed to the person server that issued the person token.

example.note: This delivers the same resource token that the authorization-endpoint scenario returns in a response body, inside the challenge instead.

steps.label: POST auth_token_endpoint w/ resource_token + presented_token
steps.description: The agent brings the resource token to its PS, along with the person token it presented to the resource and a short justification. The PS checks that agent_jkt matches the key that signed this request and that the presented token matches the resource token.

example.note: The PS checks agent_jkt against the key that signed this request (the agent's), and checks presented_token against the resource token's presented_jti, ps and sub.

body.justification: Order Fido, as the person asked

steps.curl:
# The signature headers are replayed from the example; curl cannot create HTTP message signatures.
curl -X POST 'https://ps.example/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Digest: sha-256=:ZulrBDNVbKjvJQg1Zm/ltb6Xm9ty90G4w3LQ6V+UrTI=:' \
  -H 'Prefer: wait=45' \
  -H 'Signature-Input: sig=("@method" "@authority" "@path" "signature-key" "content-digest" "content-type");created=1730217700' \
  -H 'Signature: sig=:SIGNATURE-PLACEHOLDER:' \
  -H 'Signature-Key: sig=jwt;jwt="eyJhbGciOiJFZDI1NTE5IiwidHlwIjoiYWEtYWdlbnQrand0Iiwia2lkIjoiYXAta2V5LTEifQ.eyJpc3MiOi…"' \
  --data-raw '{"resource_token":"eyJhbGciOiJFZDI1NTE5IiwidHlwIjoiYWEtcmVzb3VyY2Urand0Iiwia2lkIjoicmVzb3VyY2Uta2V5LTEifQ..SIGNATURE","presented_token":"eyJhbGciOiJFZDI1NTE5IiwidHlwIjoiYWEtcGVyc29uK2p3dCIsImtpZCI6InBzLWtleS0xIn0..SIGNATURE","justification":"Summarize this quarter'\''s planning documents"}'

steps.label: 202 interaction required (url, code)
steps.description: The person server needs the person's consent before it can answer. It replies 202 Accepted with an interaction URL and a short code, and a pending URL the agent can poll.

example.note: The PS needs the person before it can issue. The agent sends the person to the interaction URL with the code and polls the Location URL.

steps.label: Open interaction URL with code
steps.description: The agent sends the person to the PS's interaction page with the code, opening a browser or showing a link or QR code.

steps.label: Review and approve
steps.description: The person reviews what is being asked: which agent, which resource, what access, and the agent's stated reason, shown as the agent's claim rather than the PS's. They approve.

steps.label: GET pending URL (Prefer: wait)
steps.description: Meanwhile the agent polls the pending URL with a signed GET, asking the PS to wait up to 45 seconds for an answer. Once the person approves, the response to this poll carries the result.

example.note: Polling switches to GET on the Location URL and does not resend the original body. Prefer: wait asks the PS to hold the response until it can answer.

steps.curl:
# The signature headers are replayed from the example; curl cannot create HTTP message signatures.
curl 'https://ps.example/pending/f7a3b9c' \
  -H 'Prefer: wait=45' \
  -H 'Signature-Input: sig=("@method" "@authority" "@path" "signature-key");created=1730217710' \
  -H 'Signature: sig=:SIGNATURE-PLACEHOLDER:' \
  -H 'Signature-Key: sig=jwt;jwt="eyJhbGciOiJFZDI1NTE5IiwidHlwIjoiYWEtYWdlbnQrand0Iiwia2lkIjoiYXAta2V5LTEifQ.eyJpc3MiOi…"'

steps.label: auth_token
steps.description: With consent given, the PS issues the auth token itself: audience the resource, the person's identifier, the granted scope, and the agent's key. It cannot outlive the person token it was issued against.

example.note: The PS issues the auth token itself (dwk aauth-person.json). Its exp does not exceed the person token's, so expires_in is shorter than an hour.

steps.label: GET /api/documents (HTTP Sig w/ auth_token)
steps.description: The agent calls the API presenting the auth token, signed with the same key.

example.note: The resource checks iss, aud, cnf against the signing key, sub and scope.

steps.curl:
# The signature headers are replayed from the example; curl cannot create HTTP message signatures.
curl 'https://resource.example/api/documents' \
  -H 'Signature-Input: sig=("@method" "@authority" "@path" "signature-key");created=1730217730' \
  -H 'Signature: sig=:SIGNATURE-PLACEHOLDER:' \
  -H 'Signature-Key: sig=jwt;jwt="eyJhbGciOiJFZDI1NTE5IiwidHlwIjoiYWEtYXV0aCtqd3QiLCJraWQiOiJwcy1rZXktMSJ9.eyJpc3MiOi…"'

steps.label: 200 OK
steps.description: The resource verifies the auth token: issuer, audience, the key binding against the request signature, the person's identifier and the scope. Then it serves the request.
